findings.title: Phpinfo Use
findings.description: The phpinfo() function is used to output information about PHP's configuration, which can reveal sensitive information about the environment, such as file paths and database credentials. Removing this function call prevents potential attackers from gathering this information. This fix assumes that the phpinfo() call is not necessary for the application's functionality.
findings.cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
findings.fix_hint: Remove the phpinfo() function call to prevent information disclosure

findings.title: Tainted Sql String
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to SQL injection because it directly inserts user input into the SQL query. Using prepared statements with parameter binding ensures that user input is treated as data, not as part of the SQL code. This prevents an attacker from injecting malicious SQL code and reduces the risk of data theft or manipulation.

findings.fix_hint: Use prepared statements to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities

attack_chains.title: SQLi to RCE
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses SQL injection to extract database credentials, then uses these credentials to gain remote code execution via a vulnerable exec function. This allows them to persist on the system and potentially exfiltrate sensitive data.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses SQL injection (finding 6a6431d3 in file vulnerabilities/bac/source/low.php) to extract database credentials
Step 2: attacker uses extracted credentials to gain remote code execution via a vulnerable exec function (finding 292c3c8c in file vulnerabilities/exec/source/high.php)
attack_chains.remediation: Input validation and sanitization for SQL queries in vulnerabilities/bac/source/low.php

attack_chains.title: PHPInfo to SQLi
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses phpinfo to reveal database configuration, then uses this information to perform SQL injection and extract sensitive data. This allows them to gain access to sensitive information and potentially use it for further attacks.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses phpinfo (finding 6a6431d3 in file phpinfo.php) to reveal database configuration
Step 2: attacker uses revealed configuration to perform SQL injection (finding 96eaf83f in file vulnerabilities/bac/source/low.php) and extract sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Remove or restrict access to phpinfo.php

attack_chains.title: Tainted Exec to Persistence
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses a tainted exec function to gain remote code execution, then uses this access to persist on the system and potentially exfiltrate sensitive data. This allows them to maintain access to the system and continue to exploit vulnerabilities.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses tainted exec (finding 292c3c8c in file vulnerabilities/exec/source/high.php) to gain remote code execution
Step 2: attacker uses gained access to persist on the system and potentially exfiltrate sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Input validation and sanitization for exec functions in vulnerabilities/exec/source/high.php
